posts.author: Prescott
posts.body:
The best way to do translations is to make a translation patch that requires someone to get the copy of the game themselves, then apply your patch. This could be done by only providing files which you have modified, usually Database and Map data files if you're just doing stuff like text. That way, you don't have to distribute any graphics which could be the cause for concern with IP holders.
I'm not an expert at law
or anything like that, but there is a good chance that you'll be fine doing it this way
(not legal advice)
. I think that, at least in the US, providing a translation for something without providing the work itself is completely fine, since the translation is more or less worthless without everything else required to make it work.
I'm not sure if this exists with RM2K, but there is the Translation++ tool for later RPG Makers that let you translate very easily and apply patches without distributing the rest of the game files. Perhaps there is something like that for RM2K as well, though I think you'd be fine just distributing the data files without the rest of the game.
Fan translations from Japanese to English are something that have been extremely common in not only the RPG Maker community but just in general for a very long time. I wouldn't worry too much about it.

That's exactly what I said. At least for 2K and 2K3, you definitely need to share the modified data but not the audio and images, unless you were translating those as well (like any text in images or voice lines). However, with newer RPG Makers, you can use Translator++ and administer patch files that way. Though, I'm not sure if this works on encrypted games or not.
Either way, doing this does at least circumvent the idea that you are redistributing someone else's game, which is made doubly awkward when it also involves content from 3rd party rights holders. All you're doing is editing text and those text edits can't stand on their own, they need to be incorporated with the rest of the game to be of any use to anyone.
There are also some data files you wouldn't even have to provide (such as Tileset data), which means the game
really
won't work if you don't already have them.
Andar said:
Unfortunately that was the past, and mostly because the japanese didn't care about the rest of the world then.
However since then the increased costs of production made the international markets more important to them, and several gaming companies made international partnerships.
And especially Disney has been known to send their sharks (read: lawyers) at the slightest hint of copyright infringment, including if said infringement was done to one of their japanese partners.
Click to expand...
We're talking about a random indie abandonware game from over a decade ago, minimum. This isn't a game that just came out by a massive company. Not to mention, these companies usually include translations for most places they plan on selling the game. Even then, translations of brand new games are routinely made, including things like uncensored patches, and correct me if I'm wrong but I don't believe I've ever seen a simple translation patch get the axe from any company.
As long as you aren't providing the game with the patch,
you should be fine.
I really don't know why this is even a topic being brought up when gaming circles, and notably RPG Maker circles, have been translating games from Japanese since they existed. There are massive translations for games like Breath of the Wild into Brazilian Portuguese, the very notable translation of Mother 3 which hasn't even had a release outside of Japan, and an active and dedicated group of people translating Phantasy Star Online 2 into English despite it having official translations.
As for RPG Maker examples, there's tons of them too. Most recently, this tends to happen with Japanese eroges, but then you have someone like VG Person who has translated games like Ib, Mad Father, Misao, Re:Kinder, Mogeko Castle, and the Witch's House. In fact, VG Person would even go on to be paid for official translations of several of these games. Other games like Corpse Party Zero, Ao Oni, Peret Em Heru, and even Toilet In Wonderland... all of these games were translated into English by dedicated members of the RPG Maker community and I see absolutely no reason why this project should be treated any differently.

Translator++ doesn't work with anything earlier than RMXP. So you need to go into the game files and change them.
You're not cooked. If you're needing to translate images too, just include the ones you have translated in the patch. That's all. Essentially, you'll just be distributing some key data files and only the images you have translated. Then, the user will drag them over the top of their own copy of the game they have downloaded, and replace the files. Easy!
If there are images that need to be translated which have copyright material in them, such as other characters or whatever, perhaps you could find a way to either get rid of those characters or change them to something else. Earthbound's localization actually did this with a truck that looked like the Coca Cola logo so that they wouldn't run into legal issues in the US.
Alternatively, you could display your patched version on top of the old one, where your patch leaves the place with the copyrighted material empty. That way, you're only distributing the pure text instead of any other graphics that exist on it. Since you'll already be providing the data file for the map in which the change to the message commands took place, you could make any changes to other event commands as well to include pictures.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Look, there are 2 ways you can translate a game:
1: You take the game, and then translate everything in it, then export it as a translated version of the game.
2: You make a patch that contains only the translation, then share that patch for others to use in their copy of the game. This means they would still need the original game.
If you translate the game itself as done in option 1, then you have to share the full game in order to share the translation. Or at least all the data files.
I guess if you make a patch, you are pretty much okay. If you can do that, than that should be fine, since you don't share the original assets. (Although a translation of a story/text, is still a copyrighted piece.)

If the game you want to translate is already using stolen content, then it is still stolen content, isn't it? Even if they share their stolen content for free, and tell you to edit it, it would still be stolen content.
If I steal a bike, and then you steal that bike from me, you still stole a bike. Just because you stole from a thief, doesn't mean you're not a thief. It just means we're both thieves. And the bike would still be a stolen bike. No matter if we customize it, pimp it up, paint it pink and fix the breaks, it will still be a stolen bike.
And the exact same thing goes for content. If you edit stolen content, it is still stolen content. If you share it and others take it, then they have stolen content too, maybe even without knowing it if you forgot to tell them.
We all make blunders and mistakes sometimes and we all get it wrong every now and then. But it doesn't make us look stupid, unless we first tell everyone how smart we are.
Anyhow... The laws around it are very vague and open for discussion, but the forum rules clearly state that copyright infringement, specially within the community itself, is a hard no-no. We're not quick to judge. We just actually happen to know a thing or two about copyright. Mainly because there have been huge debates about it in the past, where everyone tried to proof everyone else wrong, so you can trust us when we say we did out homework.
Btw... We're not judging the OP at all. We are helping the OP, or at least attempting to.
